This afternoon, I had the honor of joining my friends at the @acog during their 43rd Annual Congressional Leadership Conference. These medical professionals are the backbone of maternal healthcare, and I will always stand with them in the fight to protect the lives of mothers and babies.

The United States has the highest maternal mortality rate among high-income nations. In 2021 alone, 1,205 mothers lost their lives to pregnancy-related causes—a crisis that demands urgent action.

We know research can uncover the root causes of this crisis and lead to real solutions. That’s why I’m fighting to advance maternal health research through the bipartisan NIH IMPROVE Act—permanently authorizing funding for IMPROVE and ensuring NIH has the resources needed to continue its vital work.

Our OB-GYNs are on the front lines of this fight every day, providing the care that keeps moms and babies healthy. I will always support them, push for the resources they need, and work to ensure they can continue delivering the highest standard of care.

At yesterday’s @WaysandMeansGOP Health Subcommittee Hearing on After the Hospital: Ensuring Access to Quality Post-Acute Care, I highlighted a critical issue facing our PA-1 community: a severe shortage of healthcare staff. This crisis is leaving our patients without care or care that falls short of their needs. Skilled Nursing Facilities (SNF) are being hit hardest, with Pennsylvania projected to face the most severe staffing shortage by 2026, and half our state’s healthcare providers planning to close or sell at least 1 of their SNF locations this year.

I turned to Dr. Dana Madison, DNP, MBA, BSN, RN of Compassion Home Health Care, to share how staffing shortages have impacted patient care. She emphasized the critical role telehealth can play in bridging this gap. Telehealth has already begun to transform healthcare, making it more accessible for patients while easing the burden on providers. We must expand, not limit, access to this vital tool.

That’s why I introduced the Telehealth Expansion Act of 2025. This bipartisan legislation will allow over 32 million Americans with High-Deductible Health Plans (HDHPs) and Health Savings Accounts (HSAs) to access telehealth services before meeting their deductible—giving families the care they need when they need it most.

Watch our exchange below: ⬇️

Had a great meeting with Caroline Litchfield, CFO of @Merck, and Joseph Wolk, CFO of @JNJNews—two leaders at the forefront of medical innovation—on strengthening U.S. leadership in this critical field. As healthcare challenges grow, investing in research and development isn’t just necessary—it’s lifesaving. Innovation drives new treatments and cures, ensuring patients receive the highest quality care.

They highlighted how the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act has expanded R&D, created jobs, and driven major investments in Pennsylvania and across the country, while also protecting our biopharmaceutical industry from foreign takeovers and reinforcing America’s role in cutting-edge healthcare advancements.

Thank you, Caroline and Joseph, for your time and insight. We must continue championing policies that fuel medical breakthroughs, strengthen our economy, and ensure everyone in our community and nationwide has access to the affordable, high-quality care they deserve.

Great meeting with PA-1 community members Dr. Pamela Goldman of Yardley, along with osteopathic medical students Danielle Lapierre of Levittown and Surali Panchani of North Wales—dedicated members of the @AOAforDOs—for a timely discussion on the challenges facing our healthcare system today.
 
We focused on two major priorities: the shortage of healthcare professionals and the need to expand access to telehealth. These issues go hand in hand, and addressing them is essential to strengthening care in our community and nationwide.
 
That’s why I’m advancing bipartisan solutions like the Telehealth Expansion Act, which would give over 32 million Americans with high-deductible plans access to virtual care, and the Medicare Patient Access and Practice Stabilization Act of 2025, to give providers the stability they need to continue serving patients effectively.
 
I’m grateful to Dr. Goldman, Danielle, and Surali for their insights and the work they're doing in our community. I look forward to carrying their perspectives with me as I continue working to ensure healthcare professionals have the resources and support they need to provide high-quality care to every American.

Too many Americans hear the words “you have cancer”—when it’s already too late.

We can change that.

This week, I introduced the bipartisan SCREENS Act to ensure more women get the screenings they need before it’s too late—no matter their income, insurance status, or zip code.

Here’s what this legislation does:

➡️ Reauthorizes and expands funding—$235 million annually through 2030—for the National Breast and Cervical Cancer Early Detection Program

➡️ Covers lifesaving screenings for low-income and underinsured women

➡️ Drives early detection with proven, evidence-based strategies

➡️ Modernizes the program to meet today’s prevention and detection needs

As Co-Chair of the House Cancer Caucus, I’m fighting to remove barriers and put early detection within reach for every woman.

Read more here: ⬇️
https://t.co/YDCXFG9rav

I come from a family of nurses, and I’ve seen the grit, grace, and strength it takes to answer that call. They aren’t just essential—they are the front line and heart of our healthcare system.

That’s why I don’t just celebrate them during National Nurses Week—I fight for them every day. I’m leading the Nurse Corps Tax Parity Act to eliminate unjust tax penalties on those serving in our most underserved communities, advancing the Workplace Violence Prevention Act to keep them safe, and pushing for the support, funding, and training they need to keep doing what they do best—saving lives.

To the nurses of PA-1 and across America—thank you. This week and always, I honor you, I stand with you, and I’ll continue fighting for you.

This morning, I sat down with some of our region’s top healthcare leaders—President/CEO Doug Hughes and SVP/COO Mark Horne of @GVHHealth, @mystlukes East Region & Anderson President Ed Nawrocki, Upper Bucks & Quakertown Campus President Dennis Pfleiger, Scott Wolfe CFO of St. Luke’s University Health Network, and Melissa Shafer, who leads Government & Community Relations at St. Luke’s. We had a focused discussion about Medicaid, the needs of our hospital systems, and what it takes to ensure every patient—no matter their circumstances—has access to high-quality, affordable care.
 
From the start, I’ve been clear: no cuts to Medicare. No reductions to FMAP. No per capita caps on Medicaid. I held the line—and the initial version of the reconciliation bill reflects that. Medicaid funding will increase every year through 2034, protecting critical services for our most vulnerable neighbors.

With the bill now in the Senate, I’m working with my colleagues to push for constructive changes—safeguarding access and ensuring long-term solvency for our most vulnerable are non-negotiable. 
 
I’m grateful to our local healthcare leaders for their insight and partnership as we continue this work. Their voices are critical in shaping bipartisan, patient-centered solutions I champion that strengthen our healthcare system, support our providers, expand access, and lower costs—for every family in our community.

PA-1 families depend on and deserve strong, reliable care—and that starts with supporting the people and facilities that provide it.

Great meeting today with the @PHCA_Cares and local leaders from CommuniCare and @SaberHCG —who operate Silver Lake Healthcare in Bristol and Langhorne Gardens and Statesman in Langhorne.

We discussed the urgent challenges facing our nursing homes including workforce shortages, rising costs, and the growing strain on care delivery, and how I can continue to support them. 

Grateful to Gabrielle Charnowitz, VP of Government Affairs & Strategic Development at CommuniCare; Cody Meenan, Regional VP of Operations at Saber Healthcare; Beth Beiler, Regional Director of Business Development at Saber Healthcare; and Zach Shamberg, President & CEO of PHCA for their partnership and leadership. I look forward to continuing our work together to look forward to continuing our work to advance solutions that protect our seniors, support our caregivers, and strengthen care across our community.

Cyberattacks are hitting our hospitals harder than ever—putting lives at risk, exposing patient data, and straining care delivery.

After meeting with healthcare leaders across our community who raised the alarm, I introduced the bipartisan Healthcare Cybersecurity Act in direct partnership with providers on the frontlines.

The bill strengthens coordination between CISA and HHS, expands cybersecurity training, and equips hospitals with the tools to detect and stop threats in real time.

This is about protecting patients, defending care, and ensuring our healthcare system is ready for the threats of today—and tomorrow.

Great meeting this morning with representatives from the @APTA_official, including PA-1 community members Mason Fisher of North Wales, Daniel Freeman of Doylestown, and Carol Wamsley of Levittown.

We focused on where strategic reform is most needed: updating Medicare to reflect the true value of physical therapy, embedding fall prevention into routine care, and closing the postpartum therapy gap that continues to leave too many women without essential support. These are practical, high-impact fixes and long overdue.

When policy is shaped by experts from our own community, we get better outcomes. Grateful for our continued partnership to advance real, targeted solutions that strengthen care from the ground up.

At today’s @WaysandMeansGOP hearing, I spoke about the critical need to protect and strengthen Medicare Advantage—a program that now covers over half of all seniors on Medicare.

In Pennsylvania, MA beneficiaries save over $3,000 a year on average and experience 70% fewer hospital readmissions compared to traditional Medicare.

I have been, and will continue to be, firm in my efforts to protect and improve essential programs like Medicare Advantage because they deliver real results for our seniors.

Today, I asked Alignment Health CEO Dawn Maroney how integrated care is improving patient outcomes, and Dr. Brian Miller how we can reduce administrative burdens like prior authorization that delay care and drain provider resources.

The evidence is undeniable: Medicare Advantage is essential, it works, and it can and must be strengthened—not sidelined.

Watch our full exchange below ⬇️

Today at the Ways and Means Committee markup, I spoke in strong support of H.R. 842, the Nancy Gardner Sewell Medicare Multi-Cancer Early Detection Screening Coverage Act—introduced by my friend, @RepTerriSewell, and which I’m proud to co-sponsor.

This bipartisan bill ensures that Medicare covers FDA-approved multi-cancer early detection (MCED) tests without delay, giving seniors timely access to cutting-edge screening that can detect dozens of cancers—often before symptoms appear.

As Co-Chair of the Congressional Cancer Caucus, this fight is personal. I’ve made it my mission to advance earlier detection, faster access, and smarter cancer policy. We have the science. We have the technology. What we need now is urgency.

We cannot let red tape stand in the way of a second chance.

H.R. 842 is how we change the story.

Let’s pass this bill. And let’s make early detection the standard—not the exception.

Last week, I called on Senate Majority Leader Thune and Minority Leader Schumer to work directly with our Problem Solvers Caucus to address the rising cost of healthcare, specifically for lower- and middle-income families, with a bipartisan solution built to pass and built to last.

I joined Brian Kilmeade this morning to discuss the work underway and more.

Watch below ⬇️

Modernizing care coordination for Medicare patients has been one of my top health care priorities—and yesterday’s Ways & Means Health Subcommittee hearing underscored exactly why this work must continue.

Chronic disease now defines the Medicare population. Yet instead of coordinated care, seniors are facing:

✔️50% more specialist visits than two years ago
✔️ Thousands in preventable costs per patient
✔️ Physicians stretched too thin to focus on quality care

I focused my questioning to Dr. Michael Hoben and Dr. Ashish Parikh on two reforms I’ve been driving:

1️⃣ Making telehealth a permanent pillar of chronic care
2️⃣ Modernizing Medicare’s physician payment system

Their message was clear:

✔ Telehealth is a core tool for stabilizing chronic disease, avoiding emergencies, and lowering costs
✔ Value-based models measurably improve outcomes—from higher screening rates to fewer hospitalizations—while saving Medicare money

When telehealth payments briefly lapsed during the shutdown, we saw how quickly access can be disrupted. Permanent telehealth reliability and a modern payment system must remain central to this work, and I will continue driving it forward.

From the beginning, I’ve been clear: we would pursue a serious, two-party solution on healthcare and ACA tax credits, and we would see it through.

This plan reflects that work. It is the strongest path to 218 and 60, shaped by input from both chambers, both parties, and the White House. It directs support where families need it most and prevents catastrophic premium spikes.

When the stakes are this high, 80% of something is always better than 100% of nothing.

We will move this forward with support from both parties. Two-party solutions is what we do.  

🔗: https://t.co/pgIKq9Y9cy

I joined CNN’s @mkraju to discuss the status of our bipartisan legislation to address the rising costs of healthcare.  Our bipartisan plan protects families from higher costs and keeps the coverage they rely on affordable. It’s been built the right way—across the aisle and across chambers—with a pathway to 218 and 60 in mind.

Families need a fix, and that’s what we’re bringing to the floor. 

🔗: https://t.co/Z8U4hZSoiM

￼

I joined @MikeEmanuelFox this morning to discuss our bipartisan solution I’m advancing this week to protect families from higher healthcare costs.

We must focus on legislation that can pass — not political messaging. Our plan reflects true compromise—Democrats and Republicans, both chambers, and the White House—to deliver a fix that is responsible, realistic, and ready to move.

We have the ability to fix this, and I will continue driving this forward to do just that.

🔗: https://t.co/b2kUWRPo78

From the outset, I committed to delivering a bipartisan solution to prevent end-of-year ACA premium spikes—and today, alongside a bipartisan group of lawmakers, we are doing exactly that.

Our Bipartisan Health Insurance Affordability Act keeps ACA premium tax credits in place so families aren’t blindsided by sudden, unaffordable increases in the coverage they rely on. It’s a practical, people-first fix that prevents an immediate crisis and protects families now while preserving the space to keep working toward a stronger, smarter, more affordable healthcare system.

Responsible governance means securing 80 percent of what families need today rather than risking 100 percent of nothing tomorrow. We built this the right way, with input from across the aisle and across chambers, with the clearest pathway to the President’s desk. We’re ready to get this done, and we call on our colleagues to step up, join us, and put American families—not political messaging—first.

🔗 Read More: https://t.co/pfTz7QG4UH

This morning, I joined CNBC’s Squawk Box with my fellow @ProbSolvCaucus Co-Chair @RepTomSuozzi to discuss my Bipartisan Health Insurance Affordability Act. Yesterday, we filed a discharge petition to ensure the House has both the opportunity and the obligation to vote. Every member must decide whom they serve: the people, or the politics.

Our bill delivers:

✔️ A 2-year extension of ACA premium tax credits preventing a major premium spike and providing the runway to improve our healthcare system for the long term. 
✔️ Targeted relief for working families by restoring income limits. Unlike current law, subsidies will no longer flow to high earners.
✔️ Real PBM reform to bring accountability to the intermediaries inflating prescription drug prices.
✔️ Modernized HSAs that put individuals back in control:
— Unlike current law, HSA dollars can be used to pay premiums.
— Unlike current law, unused HSA funds roll over every year.

For months, I’ve worked with Republicans and Democrats in both chambers, with input from the Administration, to build a two-party, responsible, realistic solution that can actually pass—not a messaging bill.

This is the moment for Congress to choose whether it will protect working families or permit a crisis we can stop.
I’m firmly on the side of the American people, and I urge my colleagues to join us.

Yesterday, U.S. service members were attacked in Syria, killing three Americans. Having served in the region as a counter-terrorism agent and now on the House Intelligence Committee, I joined Jon Scott to discuss our response, as well as my Bipartisan Health Insurance Affordability Act, and our efforts to deliver targeted relief to middle- and low-income families.

🔗 Watch our full conversation here: https://t.co/XIJZrCHy8l
